# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (use these instead of source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: SKINNY McCORD (Percy Keese Fitzhugh, Gutenberg 76477, 1928, Grosset & Dunlap; illus. Howard L. Hastings; frontispiece "He groped blindly for the projecting tree")

### Chapter list
I Skinny Loses Something; II Shadows; III Ears that Hear; IV By the Dead Fire; V Face to Face; VI In the Dim Light; VII Dark Plans; VIII Stealth; IX For Danny; X Won; XI If; XII Scout Law Number Two; XIII Alias Danville Bently; XIV The Pioneer Scout; XV The Serenade; XVI The Accused; XVII The Masquerader; XVIII To Pastures New; XIX The New Arrival; XX Skinny's Protégé; XXI Temple Camp Takes Notice; XXII Partners; XXIII Henny's Cave; XXIV Missing; XXV From Above; XXVI With the Smoke; XXVII Skinny's Hero; XXVIII It Runs in the Family; XXIX Just as Easy--; XXX Fixed; XXXI Holly Hollis; XXXII The Night Before; XXXIII Victory and Then--; XXXIV The Price

### Characters
- **Skinny McCord** (Alfred McCord), small, shy, bashful, sensitive "gnome"/mascot of the Elk Patrol, First Bridgeboro Troop, Martha Norris Memorial Cabins. Lives in Corkscrew Alley, Bridgeboro NJ; father works paper mill; mother dead? (Danny's mother dead; Skinny is child of Mr. McCord's second wife). Lacks scout suit at first; bought suit at Kingston with Curry (assistant scoutmaster, drove Ford); suit too big. Weighs 64 lbs. Wears no-fit shabby clothes, sneakers/bare feet. Has a compass (lost at camp-fire, chap I; sought in dark). Has private shanty retreat in old railroad cut with red lantern.
- **Danny McCord** (Danville "Danny" McCord), Skinny's half-brother (different mothers); escaped Blythedale Boys' Home (reform school) after escapade with Mr. Burt's Ford; licked Dick Kinney of Irontown (who took Skinny's ball, said he was "quarter of a brother"); escaped by grape-vine, ice-tongs, cord; hitched rides, arrived Temple Camp ~51 miles from Blythedale. Impersonates Danville Bently (Florida, Wave Crest City; father Roswell T. Bently; Bently's Family Hotel). Enrolled as Danville Bently; registered as pioneer scout in Pioneer Row; wore Skinny's suit. Punched Vic Norris (Elk) for calling Skinny slum rat; punched Ralph Warner (Silver Fox) — didn't; Holman Sharpe took blame. Expelled by Councilor Wainwright with $70 (returned $30 balance; billed $40). Left to hike around lake to catch train at 6:32. Later rescued from Henny's Cave by Danville; sends $10 from Porto Rico in November, note "Here's a ten spot, see you later about the rest. Danny." Mentions a ship/cabin boy goal; worked on ships/Porto Rico.
- **Danville Bently** (real), tall, merry, polite, southern accent, white scarf with silver ring, white belt, white hat cord; "Polar Bear" patrol of Florida; "White Scarf" nickname; joined Tent Village; ambles, nonchalant, can't be ruffled. Alias-impostor was Danny; real Bently arrives Aug 2 (bus, with Skinny meeting him). Takes Overlook Cabin on Black Hill ("twelve bucks a week") with Skinny. Says "I never get mad." Rescues Skinny and Danny from Henny's Cave; kills rattlesnake with jack-knife; uses bark + stick tourniquet; refuses Gold Cross, says "Gold Cross is only kind of like a receipt." Gives Danny $20. Helps Test Four (14-mile hike); tests first class.
- **Holman Sharpe**: pioneer scout from New Hampshire farm, studious, by-the-book; marked Handbook; English Handbook; accused of lying re Valley Creek ford; struck Ralph Warner; Danny took blame; Councilor Wainwright.
- **Roy Blakeley** (Silver Foxes), jolly ringleader; with Warde Hollister and Ralph Warner serenaded Sharpy ("Oh Sharpy, dear Sharpy...").
- **Pee-wee Harris** (mentioned); **Tom Slade** (camp assistant), **Uncle Jeb (Rushmore)** old trapper; **Brent Gaylong** (lanky); **Connie Bennett** (Elk patrol leader, Skinny's patrol leader); **Vic Norris**, **Stut Moran**, **Bert McAlpin**, **Hunt Ward** (Elks); **Howell Cross** (Eagle, First Vermont Eagles); **Ellis Carway** (Eagle); **Holly Hollis** (Eagle Scout from Bridgeboro, slim, black hair, 21 merit badges, joins Elks; drowns in marsh, saved by Skinny); **Helmer Clarkson** (rich boy, Hiawatha canoe buyer, "Sweet-dream Ellie"); **Chocolate Drop** (colored cook); **Councilor Wainwright** (Wainey), **Councilor Tenny**, **Councilor Barrows**, **Mr. Ellsworth** (scoutmaster), **Mr. Wainwright**; **Curry** (asst scoutmaster); **Charlie Avery** (Long Island new boy); **Pompy Arliss** (Brooklyn troop); **Collie Edwards** (Star Scout); **Dick Kinney** (Irontown); **Punkhead**; **Mr. Burt** (Ford owner); **Warde Hollister**, **Ralph Warner**.

### Key events (in order)
1. Camp-fire: Skinny's compass lost; teasing; Brent, Tom, Uncle Jeb discuss Skinny's suit.
2. Ch II–III: a stranger (Danny) on bench at road sign "To Temple Camp"; reads letter from Roswell T. Bently (Wave Crest City, Fla., June 27, 1927) to Board of Councilors saying son Danville delayed to August 2 (trip to Europe); Danny takes letter.
3. Ch IV: Danny at Martha Norris cabins; dead fire; meets Skinny at fire ring.
4. Ch V: Skinny leads Danny to railroad-cut shanty; Danny plans escape hiding as Bently; Skinny confesses suit purchase; Danny: "You can't hide inside of a scout if you're not a scout."
5. Ch VI–VII: Danny proposes impersonation; Skinny steals Handbook and suit from locker; Danny dresses in suit; Skinny gets pennant.
6. Ch VIII: Skinny steals White Pennant from Alligators of Alleghany cabin (skunk skin on door), barefoot, shoes around neck.
7. Ch IX: Skinny's plan to swim for Hiawatha Prize canoe; Connie orders him to wear suit; he swims lake at dawn (~fourteen-twenty); pulls off shirt; Administration Shack office hours 10-11 (rule XI).
8. Ch X: fisherman rescues Skinny; Stut Moran ties bathrobe; Bert McAlpin: train for Mary Temple Cup.
9. Ch XI: Skinny tries to sell canoe to Helmer Clarkson for $15 (worth $70); fails; "What a tragic word is IF!"
10. Ch XII: Skinny brings sandwiches and cookies to Danny; Danny reads Handbook.
11. Ch XIII: Elks confront Skinny; Vic Norris insults; Danny (as Danville) punches Vic Norris.
12. Ch XIV–XV: Danny's pioneer dormitory; Holman Sharpe; Pie Alley serenade by Roy.
13. Ch XVI–XVII: Holman strikes Ralph; Danny takes blame; expelled by Wainwright with $70; Danny returns $70 in envelope "To the Managers of Temple Camp."
14. Ch XVIII–XIX: Danny leaves; real Bently arrives Aug 2 wearing white scarf; Skinny guides him.
15. Ch XX–XXII: bulletin notice about impersonation; Bently befriends Skinny, paddles canoe; Test Four plan.
16. Ch XXIII–XXVIII: Henny's Cave trip; Danny (unknown) inside; smoke; Skinny opens hole with stick; rattlesnake coils on his leg; Danville kills snake with jack-knife on bark; rescue reveals rescued boy is Danny; Danville decides no Gold Cross; gives Danny $20.
17. Ch XXIX–XXX: Elks give up Skinny's locker key; Danville engages Overlook Cabin on Black Hill; Holly Hollis joins Elk patrol.
18. Ch XXXI–XXXIII: Eagle race (Mary Temple Cup); Elk patrol wins via Holly Hollis; Holly capsizes into marsh; Skinny tears signal easel canvas to rescue him.
19. Ch XXXIV: Holly resigns Elk patrol; Danville: "An eagle is not as high as you can go."

Fact of note: Danny's letter to Danny (postmark Porto Rico); Gold Cross not received; Danville said "Gold Cross is only kind of like a receipt."

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE YOUNG NAVAL CAPTAIN; OR THE WAR OF ALL NATIONS (Captain Ralph Bonehill [pseud. Edward Stratemeyer], Thompson & Thomas, Chicago, 1902; Gutenberg 75394)

### Chapter list
I The United States Against the World; II First Battle on the Ocean; III An Interview with the Secretary of the Navy; IV Blowing Up of the Tien-Tsin; V Prisoners of the Sea; VI Out of a Living Tomb; VII An Attack on the Japanese Troops; VIII The Act of a Madman; IX Another Blowing Up; X The Fraudulent Message; XI An Urgent Call for the Holland XI; XII Defeat Turned Into Victory; XIII The Central American Canal; XIV Cast Upon the Shore; XV Tidal Waves and Whales; XVI Saving the Merchantman; XVII Playing the Spy; XVIII The Capture of Hang Chang; XIX News of the President's Daughter; XX The Cave Under the Ocean; XXI Out of One Danger Into Another; XXII A Run Not Wanted; XXIII The Fight off Cape Nome; XXIV Sinking of the Ivan II; XXV In Which the Holland XI is Captured; XXVI Prisoners on the Holland XI; XXVII The Defeat of the Enemy; XXVIII An Underwater Earthquake; XXIX The Rescue of Jean Fevre; XXX The Last Battle--Conclusion

### Characters
- **Oscar Pelham** (captain, ~20, black eyes, curly black hair; inventor; son of Commodore David Pelham, Standard Shipyard, Bridgeport; orphan; wealth inherited). Commands the **Holland XI** (submarine; aluminum & steel; 115 ft long, 16 ft wide; 23 knots).
- **Andy Greggs** (first lieutenant, 18, blue eyes, curly brown hair, machinist; Oscar's chum).
- **George Dross** (old engineer, head engineer; "Cap'n"; dialect).
- **Marney** (air man), **Walton** (ammunition man), **Gilson** (helper), lookout.
- **Gabretti** (Italian engineer who blew up original Holland I for foreign bribe $100,000; reward $50,000; captured at Santiago).
- **President Jefferson McKinley Adams**; **Martha Adams** (daughter, kidnapped from White House; rescued from Green Dragon); **Mrs. Adams** (ill).
- **Secretary Short** (Navy Secretary); **Senator Forbish** (NY); **Commodore Garrison** (Cuba); **Admiral Fielding** (Canada/Maine); **Admiral Alvin Chester** (Pacific); **Lieutenant Raxtell** (mad, homesick, put ashore at Boston).
- **Nathan Pargloss** (dismissed Treasury man; plotted canal lock explosions; drowned at lock).
- **Hang Chang** (Chinese captain; captured on Corcoran; cave under ocean; tried to drown Oscar, killed by Andy's knife).
- **Captain Gresson** (British, Corcoran).
- **Captain Roquez** (Spanish, captured Holland XI; killed Canelli).
- **Jean Fevre** (French dude rescued from wreck Bordeaux).
- Chinese cruisers: Tien-Tsin (first, blown up), Pekin, Green Dragon (holding Martha), Shanghai.

### Key events (in order)
1. Ch I: War declared 1936 against world; Oscar and Andy; Oscar invents Holland XI; Holland I blown up by Gabretti.
2. Ch II: Naval battle off Sandy Hook; German submarine sinks US ships.
3. Ch III: Oscar interviews Secretary Short; senator's letter.
4. Ch IV: Model test; government orders new Holland in one month ($500,000); destroys Tien-Tsin at Baracoa.
5. Ch V: French cruiser Republique falls on Holland; trapped in sand; torpedo fails.
6. Ch VI: Oscar goes out in diving suit; Holland freed by explosion; Oscar nearly drowns, reaches Cuban shore.
7. Ch VII: Japanese troops capture Oscar; Andy rescues; dynamite bombs destroy Japanese column.
8. Ch VIII: Sargasso Sea entanglement; Lt. Raxtell's madness discovered.
9. Ch IX: Raxtell restrained; Holland sinks Wilhelm II, Terrible, Philippe.
10. Ch X: Kidnapping news; fraudulent messages; mine trap; ramming English despatch boat.
11. Ch XI: Anchor wrecks screw; repair; Gulf of Maine battle; "Come to Casco Bay instantly."
12. Ch XII: Holland turns defeat to victory (Coronet, Virginia, Italian/Turkish ships).
13. Ch XIII: Central American canal; Pargloss drowned.
14. Ch XIV: Honolulu capture; Holland blows up foreign ships.
15. Ch XV: Tidal wave; whales; whale stuck in trap door (Ch XVI: signal shell destroys whale head; lightning kills a man).
16. Ch XVII–XVIII: Oscar as spy "Barton Peeks"; Hang Chang captured; secret codes "Sixteen, nine."
17. Ch XIX: Hang Chang reveals Martha on Green Dragon; threatens to torture.
18. Ch XX: Pekin destroyed; anchor chain tangle; Japanese Tokio sunk by torpedo; cave under ocean; Ch XXI: sea serpent killed by dynamite shell; lightning strikes Holland; Ch XXII–XXIII: electricity fixed; Ch XXIV: Ivan II sunk at Cape Nome (~209 Russians captured, incl. Admiral).
19. Ch XXV: Hang Chang goes overboard dragging Oscar; Andy kills him; Spanish captain Roquez captures Holland at night (Walton, Dross, others); Ch XXVI–XXVII: Oscar and Andy escape; Canelli killed; Gabretti captured; Santiago de Cuba handover ($50,000 reward).
20. Ch XXVIII–XXIX: underwater volcano/earthquake in Caribbean; Jean Fevre rescued from wreck Bordeaux.
21. Ch XXX: Green Dragon found; Martha rescued (Chinese admiral shot by Oscar; Oscar shot in shoulder); Green Dragon torpedoed; war ends; Oscar becomes Rear Admiral Pelham; married Martha; Andy and Dross become commodores of squadrons.
